title: The picker puts new sessions beside earlier ones
body:
The picker in `src/picker.rs` opens on a bare `coax` launch. It stacks a `sessions` pane, listing earlier sessions for the folder, above an `agents` pane. Each agent row shows the agent's name and its full command. `j` and `k` move through the sessions and then the agents, and Enter loads a session or starts a new one on an agent.

## Proposal

Jack approved this layout:

```text
 coax · pick a session or start a new one
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
╭ new ───────────╮╭ sessions ───────────────────────────────────────╮
│ ● claude       ││ › this is a session                claude   23h │
│ ◐ codex        ││   blah blah blah                   claude    2d │
│ ✗ gemini       ││   another session                  claude nov 18│
╰────────────────╯╰─────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
 claude-agent-acp                                     ready · 4 sessions
 j/k move   h/l or tab switch   enter start   esc quit
```

- The `new` pane, holding the agents, sits on the left at the width of its longest agent name. `sessions` takes the rest, and both run the screen's full height.
- The focused pane's border and title are in the accent colour, and the other pane is dimmed. Only the focused pane shows `›` and the selection bar. `h` and `l`, or Tab, switch panes. Focus starts on the newest session, or on the `default` agent when there is none.
- Each agent's row starts with `●` in green when the agent is ready, the spinner while it starts, or a red `✗` when it failed.
- A dim line under the panes shows the selected agent's command, its status and its session count, or a failed agent's reason.
- A session row shows the title, then a dim agent name and age, right-aligned. Ages are short: `23h`, `2d`, then the date, as `nov 18`, past a week.
- A folder with no sessions shows "no earlier sessions here", dimmed, in the sessions pane. No configured agents shows the config path in the new pane.
- Enter on an agent starts a new session at once, as it does today.
